title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Termly Exam #6 (Term 3)

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #6 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is a use of gravity? (1 mark)
   A. Lifting up a stone by itself
   B. Water flowing downhill
   C. Making air hot
   D. Making objects float in air

2. Which of these is a way of reducing friction on a bicycle chain? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving it dry and rusty
   B. Adding sand
   C. Oiling it
   D. Wetting it with mud

3. A force can be small or big. A bigger push makes a ball go (1 mark)
   A. Slower
   B. Not move
   C. Faster and further
   D. Change colour

4. A rolling ball slowly comes to a stop on the ground mainly because of (1 mark)
   A. Sound
   B. Friction
   C. Light
   D. Colour

5. What should you do when doing force experiments? (1 mark)
   A. Throw heavy things
   B. Keep fingers away from moving parts
   C. Run with sharp tools
   D. Push others

6. What does a force do when it squeezes a sponge? (1 mark)
   A. Makes it lighter
   B. Makes it hot
   C. Changes its colour
   D. Changes its shape

7. Why do we put oil on machine parts? (1 mark)
   A. To reduce friction
   B. To make them heavy
   C. To make them weak
   D. To increase friction

8. You want to see if a material is opaque. What do you do? (1 mark)
   A. Weigh it
   B. Shine a torch at it and see if light passes
   C. Taste it
   D. Smell it

9. How can lights help protect a home? (1 mark)
   A. Lights make people sleep
   B. Lights make walls hot
   C. Security lights help keep thieves away
   D. Lights make doors open

10. Which of these is a way of making a room lighter during the day? (1 mark)
   A. Closing the door
   B. Painting the walls black
   C. Closing the window
   D. Opening the curtains

11. When light hits an opaque object, what forms behind it? (1 mark)
   A. A rainbow
   B. A flame
   C. A shadow
   D. Sound

12. Which battery-powered device gives artificial light? (1 mark)
   A. Stars
   B. Torch
   C. Sun
   D. Firefly

13. Which of these could you use to test three cards for straight line travel of light? (1 mark)
   A. A ruler only
   B. A cup of water
   C. A bell
   D. Cards with holes in the middle and a torch

14. Which of these is the biggest natural source of light for the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. The sun
   B. A star far away
   C. A candle
   D. The moon

15. How does heat help plants and animals? (1 mark)
   A. It makes them cold
   B. It keeps them warm enough to live
   C. It makes them sleepy
   D. It stops growth

16. Why are pot handles often made of wood or plastic? (1 mark)
   A. They get very hot
   B. They pass heat slowly
   C. They pass heat quickly
   D. They are heavy

17. In which unit is temperature measured in science? (1 mark)
   A. Metres
   B. Litres
   C. Kilograms
   D. Degrees Celsius

18. Which of these is a fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Sand
   B. Glass
   C. Firewood
   D. Clean water

19. Which instrument measures temperature? (1 mark)
   A. Ruler
   B. Thermometer
   C. Balance
   D. Measuring jug

20. Where should children be when an adult is cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Away from the fire
   B. Next to the fire
   C. On top of the cooker
   D. Holding the pot

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give two examples each of transparent and opaque materials. (2 marks)

22. Why should we use LED and solar lamps instead of paraffin lamps? Give two reasons. (4 marks)

23. Explain why the flat paper and stone dropped together do not land at the same time. (3 marks)

24. Describe how windows, roofs and walls can be used to make a house brighter by day. (4 marks)

25. Explain why light is important in our daily lives. (5 marks)

26. Describe five ways in which forces are used at home and on the farm. (5 marks)

27. Explain why cooking pots are made of metal but their handles are not. (4 marks)

28. Explain why a translucent roof sheet is useful in a classroom during the day. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #6 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Water flowing downhill
   Gravity makes water flow downhill.

2. C — Oiling it
   Oil helps parts slide.

3. C — Faster and further
   A stronger force has a bigger effect.

4. B — Friction
   Friction between the ball and the ground slows it.

5. B — Keep fingers away from moving parts
   Safe practice prevents injuries.

6. D — Changes its shape
   Squeezing changes the shape.

7. A — To reduce friction
   Oil makes surfaces slide easily.

8. B — Shine a torch at it and see if light passes
   If no light passes, it is opaque.

9. C — Security lights help keep thieves away
   Thieves avoid places where they can be seen.

10. D — Opening the curtains
   Open curtains let in more daylight.

11. C — A shadow
   Blocked light makes a shadow.

12. B — Torch
   A torch is made by people.

13. D — Cards with holes in the middle and a torch
   Aligned holes let light pass only when straight.

14. A — The sun
   The sun lights the Earth in the daytime.

15. B — It keeps them warm enough to live
   Life needs suitable warmth.

16. B — They pass heat slowly
   Handles stay cooler.

17. D — Degrees Celsius
   Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.

18. C — Firewood
   Fuels burn to give heat.

19. B — Thermometer
   A thermometer shows how hot something is.

20. A — Away from the fire
   Children stay away from the cooker.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Transparent: clear glass, clear plastic, clean water. Opaque: wood, metal, stone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pair.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: They are safer with less fire risk and less smoke. Solar lamps use free energy and are cheaper to use.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each reason.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gravity pulls both down but air pushes up on the flat paper more, so it falls slowly. The stone is little affected by the air.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for gravity on both, 1 mark for air pushing paper, 1 mark for stone landing first.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Large windows let in light, translucent roof sheets let in light, light-coloured walls reflect light, open curtains.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: It lets us see, keeps us safe, helps plants to make food, dries clothes, gives solar power and discourages pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

26. (5 marks)
   Answer: Pushing a wheelbarrow, pulling a plough, lifting water from a well with a rope, hammering a nail, kicking a ball, stitching clothes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Metal passes heat quickly to the food so it cooks. Handles made of wood or plastic pass heat slowly so our hands do not burn.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the pot and 2 marks for the handle.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: It lets daylight in, so lamps are not needed, saving electricity and money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for daylight, 1 mark for no lamps, 1 mark for saving.
